_why:
#38 — `--trunk` defaulted to the literal string `main`, so on any checkout holding the trunk only as `origin/main` (a --single-branch clone, a CI checkout, a worktree that never checked it out) the preflight raised `unknown_ref:main` and BOTH 5f and 6a-prime were unrunnable without the operator discovering `--trunk origin/main` unaided.

Its filed coupling was wrong in BOTH directions and that is the reusable part. The brief said 'same root as WSG-5': false — WSG-5 is the first-commit heuristic, reached only AFTER both refs resolve, and `3a04342` touched no line of the ref preflight. The probe then named 7f as the real sibling, which is true of the trigger and NOT of the fix: 7f's `--base` is a merge TARGET, where `git checkout origin/main` DETACHES and a measured run reported MERGED at exit 0 with the merge commit unreferenced. Here the trunk is only ever READ. Same trigger, opposite correct response — so mutation 3 exists to stop anyone 'fixing' one into the other.

mutations.name: the-remote-tracking-fallback-is-removed
mutations._mechanism: Restores the defect exactly: `unknown_ref:main` and rc=2 on a checkout whose trunk is remote-only, with 5f and 6a-prime both blocked behind it.

mutations.name: the-verdict-echoes-the-requested-trunk-not-the-measured-one
mutations._mechanism: The line would print `trunk=main` for a derivation made against `origin/main` — a verdict naming a ref it did not use. Same class as the merge-base sha this script exists to replace: a plausible wrong answer that reads exactly like a right one.

mutations.name: the-remote-ref-is-preferred-over-the-local-one
mutations._mechanism: THE silent over-correction. Between fetches a local trunk is routinely ahead of or behind its remote, so preferring `origin/main` measures a DIFFERENT commit and still prints OK. A wrong 5c sha that looks right is the original J41 defect restored by the fix for #38.

mutations.name: the-failure-does-not-say-what-it-tried
mutations._mechanism: `unknown_ref:main` on a checkout that plainly has a main reads as a bug in the tool rather than a fact about refs, and the operator has no way to learn the remote form was already considered.

mutations.name: the-branch-is-given-the-remote-fallback-too
mutations._mechanism: Scope leak. A 5c baseline is a statement about a branch in THIS checkout; resolving `feature/x` to `origin/feature/x` derives a baseline for a branch the operator is not on, cannot see, and did not ask about — and reports it as theirs at exit 0.
